items.assessment: No demonstrated paradox; pass heterogeneity is visible. E−S_low is −0.00048828125 in pass1 and +0.01806640625 in pass2. Report both descriptively without selecting a favorable pass.
Addressed by limiting the estimate to equal-weight requests. The 4,096 block/window occurrences and 59,952 valid proposal occurrences are not independent samples.
Caution: reused development requests and historical E outcomes were known. No fresh-population or independent-confirmation claim is supported.
No fitted observational conditioning model is used. Per-window norm matching deliberately conditions on E’s achieved size; inference is confined to these two experimental comparators.
Denominators checked: 4,096 paired keys, 3,577 old blockers, 3,511 old prefixes, 52 native-repair displacement opportunities. All-zero/tie requests remain.
Fixed windows and probe keys were not selected using new scalar outcomes; historical development reuse still limits broad claims. No extremal-subset efficacy claim is made.
Full five-state grid present: 20,480/20,480 valid rows, including all 8,192 new rows; no missing, invalid, dropped or duplicate keys.
All six prespecified contrasts are reported. The joint primary requires BOTH E−S intervals to have positive lower bounds; it fails. Descriptive intervals are not alternative success tests.
Scope/order/bootstrap/decision were fixed before new scoring. No post-hoc subset, tolerance or panel change is justified by this audit. Long project history and development reuse remain disclosed.

Paired one-step endpoint interventions support this local contrast, not isolation of a harmful gradient direction, an optimal LR, or improved online serving. E and native-LR endpoints can have different Adam moments.
Feedback and checkpoints precede fixed evaluation; no outcome enters calibration. Historical E sizes inform comparator selection by design and are not a deployable prediction rule.
